description: AAASM-5344: clean Thai prose — no findings. Thai is the third space-less script and sits outside the Han ranges entirely, so a CJK-codepoint-range exemption would not cover it by construction. At today's 4.5 gate that is latent rather than exploitable: Thai's UTF-8 shape (a constant E0 lead byte and only two distinct second bytes) caps its byte entropy near 3.2, so it clears the gate on entropy rather than on script — and unlike the Han vectors it does not reproduce the shipped defect. What it pins is that the ASCII-run narrowing, not the gate value, is what protects it; its 45-byte clause sits inside the 20–64 length window, so it is the vector that fails first if the gate is ever retuned downward.
